pob.text: And his brothers by their clans[a], in the genealogy of their generations: the chief was Jeiel, and Zechariah.

spob.text: And Bela was the son of Azaz. Azaz was the son of Shema, and Shema was the son of Joel. Bela lived in the area extending from Aroer as far as Nebo and Baal-meon.

pob.text: To the east he settled as far as the entrance to the wilderness from the river Euphrates[a], because their livestock had multiplied in the land of Gilead.

spob.text: He and his clan settled eastward, as far as where the wilderness begins in the region extending from the Euphrates River.[a] They did this because their livestock had become numerous in the land of Gilead.

public_domain_references.bsb: They also settled in the east as far as the edge of the desert that extends to the Euphrates River, because their livestock had increased in the land of Gilead.
public_domain_references.web: and he lived eastward even to the entrance of the wilderness from the river Euphrates, because their livestock were multiplied in the land of Gilead.

public_domain_references.brenton: And he dwelt eastward to the borders of the wilderness, from the river Euphrates: for they had much cattle in the land of Galaad.

pob.text: In the days of Saul they made war with the Hagrites[a], and they fell into their hand[b]; and they lived in their tents throughout all the region east of Gilead.

spob.text: During Saul’s reign, they fought against the Hagrites,[a] who fell into their power. Then they lived in the Hagrites’ tents throughout the whole region east of Gilead.

public_domain_references.bsb: During the days of Saul they waged war against the Hagrites, who were defeated at their hands, and they occupied the homes of the Hagrites throughout the region east of Gilead.

public_domain_references.asv: And in the days of Saul, they made war with the Hagrites, who fell by their hand; and they dwelt in their tents throughout all the [land] east of Gilead.
public_domain_references.kjv: And in the days of Saul they made war with the Hagarites, who fell by their hand: and they dwelt in their tents throughout all the east [land] of Gilead.
public_domain_references.brenton: And in the days of Saul they made war upon the sojourners [in the land]; and they fell into their hands, all of them dwelling in their tents eastward of Galaad.

pob.text: And the sons of Gad lived opposite them in the land of Bashan[b][a], as far as Salecah.

spob.text: The people of Gad lived across from them in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah.[a]

public_domain_references.brenton: The sons of Gad dwelt over against them in the land of Basan even to Sela.

pob.text: Joel the chief[a], Shapham the second, and Jaanai and Shaphat in Bashan.

spob.text: In Bashan, Joel was the chief, and Shapham was second in rank. Jaanai and Shaphat were there as well.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Jaanai and Shaphat, who lived in Bashan.
public_domain_references.web: Joel the chief, Shapham the second, Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.

public_domain_references.brenton: Joel the first-born, and Sapham the second, and Janin the scribe in Basan.

pob.text: And their brothers[a], according to their fathers’ houses: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia[d][c][b], and Eber—seven.

spob.text: Their brothers[a], listed by their ancestral family groups, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.

public_domain_references.bsb: Their kinsmen by families were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.

public_domain_references.brenton: And their brethren according to the houses of their fathers; Michael, Mosollam, and Sebee, and Joree, and Joachan, and Zue, and Obed, seven.

pob.text: These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri[a], son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.

spob.text: These were the sons of Abihail. His ancestry ran through Huri, Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz.[a]

pob.text: Ahi son of Abdiel[a], son of Guni, was head of their fathers’ houses.

pob.text: They lived in Gilead[a], in Bashan and its towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon[c][b], as far as their borders.

spob.text: They lived in Gilead and in Bashan, including Bashan’s towns. They also lived in all the pasturelands of Sharon, all the way to their outer borders.

public_domain_references.web: They lived in Gilead in Bashan and in its towns, and in all the pasture lands of Sharon as far as their borders.

public_domain_references.brenton: They dwelt in Galaad, in Basan, and in their villages, and [in] all the country round about Saron to the border.

pob.text: All of them were enrolled by genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah[a], and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

spob.text: They were all entered in genealogical records during the reign of Jotham king of Judah and during the reign of Jeroboam king of Israel.

pob.text: The sons of Reuben and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh[a], valiant men, men who carried shield and sword, who drew the bow, and who were trained for war, were forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty[c][b], able to go out to war.

spob.text: The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 valiant fighting men fit for military service. They carried shields and swords, drew bows, and were trained for war.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 warriors—valiant men who carried the shield and sword, drew the bow, and were trained for battle.
public_domain_references.web: The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, able to shoot with bow, and skillful in war, were forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty that were able to go out to war.
public_domain_references.asv: The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful in war, were forty and four thousand seven hundred and threescore, that were able to go forth to war.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sword, and to shoot with bow, and skilful in war, [were] four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore, that went out to the war.
public_domain_references.brenton: The sons of Ruben and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasse, of mighty men, bearing shields and sword, and bending the bow, and skilled in war, [were] forty and four thousand and seven hundred and sixty, going forth to battle.

pob.text: They made war against the Hagrites[a], Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

spob.text: They went to war against the Hagrites,[a] Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

public_domain_references.bsb: They waged war against the Hagrites, as well as Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
public_domain_references.web: They made war with the Hagrites, with Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
public_domain_references.asv: And they made war with the Hagrites, with Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they made war with the Hagarites, with Jetur, and Nephish, and Nodab.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they made war with the Agarenes, and Itureans, and Naphiseans, and Nadabeans,

pob.text: They were helped against them[a], and the Hagrites and all who were with them were given into their hand, because they cried out to God in the battle[c][b], and he answered them because they trusted in him.

spob.text: They received help against their enemies. The Hagrites[a] and all who were with them were handed over to them in defeat, because they cried out to God during the battle. He answered them because they trusted in him.

public_domain_references.bsb: And because they cried out to God in battle, they were helped against their enemies, and the Hagrites and all their allies were delivered into their hands. Because they put their trust in God, He answered their prayers.
public_domain_references.web: They were helped against them, and the Hagrites were delivered into their hand, and all who were with them; for they cried to God in the battle, and he answered them because they put their trust in him.
public_domain_references.asv: And they were helped against them, and the Hagrites were delivered into their hand, and all that were with them; for they cried to God in the battle, and he was entreated of them, because they put their trust in him.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they were helped against them, and the Hagarites were delivered into their hand, and all that [were] with them: for they cried to God in the battle, and he was intreated of them; because they put their trust in him.
public_domain_references.brenton: and they prevailed against them: and the Agaræans were given into their hands, [they] and all their tents: for they cried to God in the battle, and he hearkened to them, because they trusted on him.

pob.text: They captured their livestock: 50,000 camels[a], 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 people.

spob.text: They captured their livestock—50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also took 100,000 people captive.

public_domain_references.bsb: They seized the livestock of the Hagrites—50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, and 2,000 donkeys. They also took 100,000 captives,
public_domain_references.web: They took away their livestock: of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred fifty thousand, and of donkeys two thousand, and of men one hundred thousand.
public_domain_references.asv: And they took away their cattle; of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred and fifty thousand, and of asses two thousand, and of men a hundred thousand.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they took away their cattle; of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred and fifty thousand, and of asses two thousand, and of men an hundred thousand.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they took captive their store; five thousand camels, and two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, two thousand asses, and a hundred thousand men.

pob.text: For many slain fell[a], because the battle was from God; and they lived in their place until the exile.

spob.text: Many were killed in battle, because its outcome came from God. The victors then lived in the land of those they had defeated until the exile.

public_domain_references.bsb: and many others fell slain, because the battle belonged to God. And they occupied the land until the exile.
public_domain_references.web: For many fell slain, because the war was of God. They lived in their place until the captivity.
public_domain_references.asv: For there fell many slain, because the war was of God. And they dwelt in their stead until the captivity.
public_domain_references.kjv: For there fell down many slain, because the war [was] of God. And they dwelt in their steads until the captivity.
public_domain_references.brenton: For many fell slain, because the war [was] of God. And they dwelt in their place until the captivity.

pob.text: And the sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land from Bashan as far as Baal-hermon[a], Senir, and Mount Hermon[b]; they became numerous.

spob.text: The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the territory extending from Bashan as far as Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.[a] They grew numerous.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now the people of the half-tribe of Manasseh were numerous. They settled in the land from Bashan to Baal-hermon (that is, Senir, also known as Mount Hermon).
public_domain_references.web: The children of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land. They increased from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
public_domain_references.asv: And the children of the half-tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land: they increased from Bashan unto Baal-hermon and Senir and mount Hermon.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And the children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land: they increased from Bashan unto Baal-hermon and Senir, and unto mount Hermon.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the half-tribe of Manasse dwelt from Basan to Baal, Ermon, and Sanir, and [to] the mount Aërmon: and they increased in Libanus.

pob.text: These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: Epher[a], Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valor, men of renown[b], heads of their fathers’ houses.

spob.text: These were the leaders of their ancestral family groups: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were mighty warriors, well-known men, and leaders of their ancestral family groups.

public_domain_references.bsb: These were the heads of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were mighty men of valor, famous men, and heads of their families.
public_domain_references.web: These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of their fathers’ houses.

public_domain_references.kjv: And these [were] the heads of the house of their fathers, even Epher, and Ishi, and Eliel, and Azriel, and Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valour, famous men, [and] heads of the house of their fathers.
public_domain_references.brenton: And these were the heads of the houses of their families; Opher, and Sei, and Eliel, and Jeremia, and Oduia, and Jediel, mighty men of valour, men of renown, heads of the houses of their families.

pob.text: But they acted unfaithfully against the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves after the gods of the peoples of the land[b][a], whom God had destroyed before them.

spob.text: But they were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors. They prostituted themselves[a] by following the gods worshiped by the peoples of the land—the peoples God had destroyed ahead of them.

public_domain_references.bsb: But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers, and they prostituted themselves with the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.
public_domain_references.web: They trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the prostitute after the gods of the peoples of the land whom God destroyed before them.
public_domain_references.asv: And they trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the harlot after the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God destroyed before them.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them.
public_domain_references.brenton: But they rebelled against the God of their fathers, and went a-whoring after the gods of the nations of the land, whom God cast out from before them.

pob.text: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria[a], even the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he took the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan[b], to this day.

spob.text: So the God of Israel stirred the spirit of Pul, king of Assyria—the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser, king of Assyria.[a][b] The king took the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh away into exile. He brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the Gozan River, where they remained to the writer’s own day.

public_domain_references.bsb: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria (that is, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria) to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. public_domain_references.web: So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and to the river of Gozan, to this day.
public_domain_references.asv: And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river of Gozan, unto this day.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river Gozan, unto this day.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Phaloch king of Assyria, and the spirit of Thagla-phallasar king of Assyria, and carried away Ruben and Gaddi, and the half-tribe of Manasse, and brought them to Chaach, and Chabor, and to the river Gozan, until this day.

public_domain_references.asv: So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of Jehovah, even the house of the tent, by wards.
public_domain_references.kjv: So they and their children [had] the oversight of the gates of the house of the LORD, [namely], the house of the tabernacle, by wards.
public_domain_references.brenton: And these and their sons [were] over the gates in the house of the Lord, and in the house of the tabernacle, to keep watch.

pob.text: The gatekeepers were at the four directions: east[a], west, north, and south.

spob.text: The gatekeepers were on all four sides—east, west, north, and south.

public_domain_references.bsb: The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: east, west, north, and south.
public_domain_references.web: On the four sides were the gatekeepers, toward the east, west, north, and south.
public_domain_references.asv: On the four sides were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south.
public_domain_references.kjv: In four quarters were the porters, toward the east, west, north, and south.
public_domain_references.brenton: The gates were toward the four winds, eastward, westward, northward, southward.

pob.text: And their brothers in their villages were to come in every seven days[a], from time to time[b], with these.

spob.text: At regular times, their fellow Levites living in the villages were to come and join them every seven days.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Their relatives came from their villages at fixed times to serve with them for seven-day periods.
public_domain_references.web: Their brothers, in their villages, were to come in every seven days from time to time to be with them,
public_domain_references.asv: And their brethren, in their villages, were to come in every seven days from time to time to be with them:
public_domain_references.kjv: And their brethren, [which were] in their villages, [were] to come after seven days from time to time with them.
public_domain_references.brenton: And their brethren [were] in their courts, to enter in weekly from time to time with these.

pob.text: For these four mighty gatekeepers[a], who were Levites[b], were entrusted with the chambers and with the storehouses of the house of God.

spob.text: For these four capable gatekeepers were Levites. They were trusted with responsibility for the rooms and storerooms in the house of God.

public_domain_references.bsb: But the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were entrusted with the rooms and the treasuries of the house of God.
public_domain_references.web: for the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and were over the rooms and over the treasuries in God’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: for the four chief porters, who were Levites, were in an office of trust, and were over the chambers and over the treasuries in the house of God.
public_domain_references.kjv: For these Levites, the four chief porters, were in [their] set office, and were over the chambers and treasuries of the house of God.
public_domain_references.brenton: For four strong [men] have the charge of the gates; and the Levites were over the chambers, and they keep watch over the treasures of the house of God.

pob.text: They spent the night around the house of God[a], because the duty of guarding it was upon them, and they were in charge of opening it morning by morning.

spob.text: They spent the night around the house of God because they were responsible for guarding it. They also had to open it each morning.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: They would spend the night stationed around the house of God, because they were responsible for guarding it and opening it every morning.
public_domain_references.web: They stayed around God’s house, because that was their duty; and it was their duty to open it morning by morning.
public_domain_references.asv: And they lodged round about the house of God, because the charge [thereof] was upon them; and to them pertained the opening thereof morning by morning.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And they lodged round about the house of God, because the charge [was] upon them, and the opening thereof every morning [pertained] to them.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the charge [was] upon them, and these [were] charged with the keys to open the doors of the temple every morning.

pob.text: Some of them were in charge of the vessels of service[a], for they brought them in by count and took them out by count.

spob.text: Some of them were responsible for the equipment used in the temple service. They counted the items when they brought them in and when they took them out.

public_domain_references.bsb: Some of them were in charge of the articles used in worship, to count them whenever they were brought in or taken out.
public_domain_references.web: Certain of them were in charge of the vessels of service, for these were brought in by count, and these were taken out by count.
public_domain_references.asv: And certain of them had charge of the vessels of service; for by count were these brought in and by count were these taken out.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [certain] of them had the charge of the ministering vessels, that they should bring them in and out by tale.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [some] of them [were appointed] over the vessels of service, that they should carry them in by number, and carry them out by number.

pob.text: And some of them were appointed over the vessels[a], over all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.

spob.text: Some of them were appointed to take care of the temple utensils and all the sacred articles, as well as the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.

public_domain_references.bsb: Others were put in charge of the furnishings and other articles of the sanctuary, as well as the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
public_domain_references.web: Some of them also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
public_domain_references.asv: Some of them also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, and over the fine flour, and the wine, and the oil, and the frankincense, and the spices.
public_domain_references.kjv: [Some] of them also [were] appointed to oversee the vessels, and all the instruments of the sanctuary, and the fine flour, and the wine, and the oil, and the frankincense, and the spices.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [some] of them [were] appointed over the furniture, and over all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.

pob.text: And some of the sons of the priests were compounders of the ointment of spices[a].

spob.text: Some members of the priestly families prepared the ointment for use with aromatic spices.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And some of the sons of the priests mixed the spices.
public_domain_references.web: Some of the sons of the priests prepared the mixing of the spices.
public_domain_references.asv: And some of the sons of the priests prepared the confection of the spices.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [some] of the sons of the priests made the ointment of the spices.
public_domain_references.brenton: And some of the priests were makers of the ointment, and [appointed to prepare] the spices.

pob.text: And Mattithiah[a], from the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite[b], was entrusted with the work of the flat cakes.

spob.text: Mattithiah was a Levite and the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite. He was entrusted[a] with preparing the flat cakes.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the bread.
public_domain_references.web: Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that were baked in pans.
public_domain_references.asv: And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, who was the first-born of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that were baked in pans.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Mattithiah, [one] of the Levites, who [was] the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, had the set office over the things that were made in the pans.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Matthathias of the Levites, (he [was] the first-born of Salom the Corite,) [was set] in charge over the sacrifices of meat-offering of the pan belonging to the high priest.

pob.text: And some of the sons of the Kohathites[a], from among their brothers, were in charge of the bread of the arrangement, to prepare it Sabbath by Sabbath.

spob.text: Some members of the Kohathite clan, chosen from among their fellow Levites, were responsible for preparing the bread set out in order every Sabbath.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Some of their Kohathite brothers were responsible for preparing the rows of the showbread every Sabbath.
public_domain_references.web: Some of their brothers, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the show bread, to prepare it every Sabbath.
public_domain_references.asv: And some of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, were over the showbread, to prepare it every sabbath.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [other] of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, [were] over the shewbread, to prepare [it] every sabbath.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Banaias the Caathite, from among their brethren, [was set] over the shewbread, to prepare it every sabbath.

pob.text: These were the singers[a], heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites, in the chambers, free from other duties, for they were occupied in the work day and night.

spob.text: These singers were leaders of the Levites’ ancestral families. They were in the rooms and were exempt from other duties,[a] because this work was their responsibility day and night.

public_domain_references.bsb: Those who were musicians, the heads of Levite families, stayed in the temple chambers and were exempt from other duties because they were on duty day and night.
public_domain_references.web: These are the singers, heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, who lived in the rooms and were free from other service, for they were employed in their work day and night.
public_domain_references.asv: And these are the singers, heads of fathers’ [houses] of the Levites, [who dwelt] in the chambers [and were] free [from other service]; for they were employed in their work day and night.
public_domain_references.kjv: And these [are] the singers, chief of the fathers of the Levites, [who remaining] in the chambers [were] free: for they were employed in [that] work day and night.
public_domain_references.brenton: And these [were] the singers, heads of families of the Levites, [to whom were] established daily courses, for they were employed in the services day and night.

pob.text: These were the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites[a], according to their generations, heads[b]. These lived in Jerusalem.

spob.text: These were the chief men who headed the Levites’ ancestral clans, according to their family lines. They lived in Jerusalem.

public_domain_references.bsb: All these were heads of Levite families, chiefs according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: These were heads of fathers’ households of the Levites, throughout their generations, chief men. They lived at Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.asv: These were heads of fathers’ [houses] of the Levites, throughout their generations, chief men: these dwelt at Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.kjv: These chief fathers of the Levites [were] chief throughout their generations; these dwelt at Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.brenton: These [were] the heads of the families of the Levites according to their generations; these chiefs dwelt in Jerusalem.

pob.text: In Gibeon lived Jeiel the father of Gibeon[b][a], and his wife's name was Maacah.

spob.text: Jeiel[b] lived in Gibeon. He was the father of Gibeon,[a] and his wife was named Maacah.

public_domain_references.bsb: Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife’s name was Maacah.
public_domain_references.web: Jeiel the father of Gibeon, whose wife’s name was Maacah, lived in Gibeon.
public_domain_references.asv: And in Gibeon there dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, whose wife’s name was Maacah;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And in Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jehiel, whose wife’s name [was] Maachah:
public_domain_references.brenton: And Jeël the father of Gabaon dwelt in Gabaon; and his wife's name [was] Moöcha.

pob.text: And his firstborn son was Abdon[a], then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, and Nadab.

spob.text: His firstborn son was Abdon. His other sons were Zur, Kish, Baal[a], Ner, and Nadab.

public_domain_references.bsb: Abdon was his firstborn son, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

spob.text: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.

public_domain_references.kjv: And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth.
public_domain_references.brenton: and Gedur and [his] brother, and Zacchur, and Makeloth.

pob.text: Mikloth fathered Shimeam[a]. They also lived opposite their brothers in Jerusalem[b], with their brothers.

spob.text: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam.[a] They too lived in Jerusalem, across from their brothers and together with them.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They too lived alongside their relatives in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. They also lived with their relatives in Jerusalem, near their relatives.
public_domain_references.asv: And Mikloth begat Shimeam. And they also dwelt with their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Mikloth begat Shimeam. And they also dwelt with their brethren at Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Makeloth begot Samaa: and these dwelt in the midst of their brethren in Jerusalem, [even] in the midst of their brethren.

pob.text: Ner fathered Kish[a], and Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.

spob.text: Ner was the father of Kish. Kish was the father of Saul. Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Ner was the father of Kish, Kish was the father of Saul, and Saul was the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
public_domain_references.web: Ner became the father of Kish. Kish became the father of Saul. Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
public_domain_references.asv: And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.

public_domain_references.brenton: And Ner begot Kis, and Kis begot Saul, and Saul begot Jonathan, and Melchisue, and Aminadab, and Asabal.

pob.text: And the son of Jehonathan was Merib-baal[b][a], and Merib-baal fathered Micah.

spob.text: Jehonathan’s son was Merib-baal,[a][b] and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.

public_domain_references.bsb: The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal, who was the father of Micah.
public_domain_references.web: The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal. Merib-baal became the father of Micah.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the son of Jonathan [was] Merib-baal: and Merib-baal begat Micah.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the son of Jonathan [was] Meribaal: and Meribaal begot Micha.

pob.text: And the sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.

spob.text: And Micah’s sons were Pithon, Melech, and Tahrea.

public_domain_references.bsb: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
public_domain_references.web: The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the sons of Micah [were], Pithon, and Melech, and Tahrea, [and Ahaz].
public_domain_references.brenton: And the sons of Micha [were] Phithon and Malach, and Tharach.

pob.text: Ahaz fathered Jarah[a], and Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.

spob.text: Ahaz was the father of Jarah.[a] Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri was the father of Moza.

public_domain_references.bsb: Ahaz was the father of Jarah; Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri was the father of Moza.

public_domain_references.kjv: And Ahaz begat Jarah; and Jarah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza;
public_domain_references.brenton: And Achaz begot Jada: and Jada begot Galemeth, and Gazmoth, and Zambri; and Zambri begot Massa.

pob.text: And Moza fathered Binea[a], and his son was Rephaiah, his son Eleasah, his son Azel.

spob.text: Moza was the father of Binea. Binea was the father of Rephaiah, Rephaiah was the father of Eleasah, and Eleasah was the father of Azel.

public_domain_references.bsb: Moza was the father of Binea. Rephaiah was his son, Elasah his son, and Azel his son.

public_domain_references.kjv: And Moza begat Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Massa begot Baana, and Rhaphaïa [was] his son, Elasa his son, Esel his son.

pob.text: Azel had six sons[a], and these were their names: Azrikam his firstborn, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan[b]. These were the sons of Azel.

spob.text: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were Azel’s sons.

public_domain_references.bsb: And Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.
public_domain_references.web: Azel had six sons, whose names are Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

public_domain_references.kjv: And Azel had six sons, whose names [are] these, Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan: these [were] the sons of Azel.

pob.text: The Philistines fought against Israel[a], and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.

spob.text: The Philistines fought against Israel. The men of Israel fled from them and fell in battle on Mount Gilboa.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
public_domain_references.web: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain on Mount Gilboa.
public_domain_references.asv: Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now the Philistines fought against Israel; and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now the Philistines warred against Israel; and they fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gelbue.

pob.text: And the Philistines pursued Saul and his sons[a], and the Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.

spob.text: The Philistines relentlessly pursued Saul and his sons. The Philistines struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, Saul’s sons.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
public_domain_references.web: The Philistines followed hard after Saul and after his sons; and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.

public_domain_references.brenton: And the Philistines pursued after Saul, and after his sons; and the Philistines smote Jonathan, and Aminadab, and Melchisue, sons of Saul.

pob.text: The battle grew heavy against Saul, and the archers found him, and he was badly wounded by the archers.

spob.text: The battle pressed heavily against Saul. The archers found him and badly wounded him.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: When the battle intensified against Saul, the archers overtook him and wounded him.
public_domain_references.web: The battle went hard against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the archers.
public_domain_references.asv: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the archers.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him, and he was wounded of the archers.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the battle prevailed against Saul, and the archers hit him with bows and arrows, and they were wounded of the bows.

pob.text: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer[a], “Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and mistreat me.” But his armor-bearer was not willing, because he was very afraid[c][b]. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.

spob.text: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Pull out your sword and run me through with it. Otherwise, these uncircumcised men[a] will come and shamefully mistreat me.” His armor-bearer refused because he was terrified. So Saul took the sword and fell on it.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run it through me, or these uncircumcised men will come and torture me!” But his armor-bearer was terrified and refused to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
public_domain_references.web: Then Saul said to his armor bearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.” But his armor bearer would not, for he was terrified. Therefore Saul took his sword and fell on it.
public_domain_references.asv: Then said Saul unto his armor-bearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me. But his armor-bearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took his sword, and fell upon it.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then said Saul to his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. So Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Saul said to his armour-bearer, Draw thy sword, and pierce me through with it, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me. But his armour-bearer would not, for he was greatly afraid: so Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.

pob.text: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead[b][a], he too fell on the sword and died.

spob.text: When Saul’s armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on the sword and killed himself.

public_domain_references.bsb: When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his own sword and died.
public_domain_references.web: When his armor bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell on his sword and died.
public_domain_references.asv: And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he likewise fell upon his sword, and died.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise on the sword, and died.
public_domain_references.brenton: And his armour-bearer saw that Saul was dead, and he also fell upon his sword.

pob.text: So Saul died[a], and his three sons, and all his house died together.

spob.text: So Saul, his three sons, and all his household died together.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: So Saul died together with his three sons and all his house.
public_domain_references.web: So Saul died with his three sons; and all his house died together.
public_domain_references.asv: So Saul died, and his three sons; and all his house died together.
public_domain_references.kjv: So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house died together.
public_domain_references.brenton: So Saul died, and his three sons on that day, and all his family died at the same time.

pob.text: When all the men of Israel who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead[a], they abandoned their cities and fled[c][b]; then the Philistines came and lived in them.

spob.text: All the Israelite men in the valley[a] saw that there had been flight and that Saul and his sons were dead. They abandoned their cities and fled. Then the Philistines came and lived in those cities.

public_domain_references.bsb: When all the Israelites in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities and ran away. So the Philistines came and occupied their cities.

pob.text: And who is like your people Israel[a], one nation on the earth, whom God went to redeem for himself as a people, to make for yourself a name by great and fearsome deeds, driving out nations from before your people[b], whom you redeemed from Egypt?

pob.text: After this[a], David struck the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Gath and its surrounding towns from the hand of the Philistines.

public_domain_references.brenton: And the lot of the east gates fell to Selemias, and Zacharias: the sons of Soaz cast lots for Melchias, and the lot came out northward.

pob.text: To Obed-edom[a], the south; and to his sons, the house of stores.

spob.text: Obed-edom was assigned the south gate, and his sons were assigned the storage building.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The lot for the South Gate fell to Obed-edom, and the lot for the storehouses to his sons.
public_domain_references.web: To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse.
public_domain_references.asv: To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the store-house.
public_domain_references.kjv: To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the house of Asuppim.
public_domain_references.brenton: To Abdedom [they gave by lot] the south, opposite the house of Esephim.

pob.text: For Shuppim and Hosah[a], the lot fell to the west, with the Gate of Shallecheth on the ascending highway, guard corresponding to guard.

spob.text: Shuppim and Hosah were assigned by lot to the west side, by the Gate of Shallecheth[a] on the road that goes uphill. Guard duty corresponded to guard duty.

public_domain_references.bsb: The lots for the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the ascending highway fell to Shuppim and Hosah. There were guards stationed at every watch.
public_domain_references.web: To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
public_domain_references.asv: To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goeth up, watch against watch.
public_domain_references.kjv: To Shuppim and Hosah [the lot came forth] westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward.
public_domain_references.brenton: [They gave the lot] for the second to Osa westward, after the gate of the chamber by the ascent, watch against watch.

pob.text: On the east were six Levites; on the north[a], four a day; on the south, four a day; and at the storehouses, two by two.

spob.text: Six Levites were assigned to the east side. Each day, four were assigned to the north side and four to the south side. At the storehouses,[a] they were assigned in pairs.

public_domain_references.bsb: Each day there were six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two pairs at the storehouse.
public_domain_references.web: Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two.
public_domain_references.asv: Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the store-house two and two.
public_domain_references.kjv: Eastward [were] six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and toward Asuppim two [and] two.
public_domain_references.brenton: Eastward [were] six [watchmen] in the day; northward four by the day; southward four by the day; and two at the Esephim,

pob.text: For the Parbar on the west: four at the road[b][a], and two at the Parbar.

spob.text: At the western area called the Parbar,[a] four gatekeepers were stationed by the road and two at the Parbar itself.

public_domain_references.bsb: As for the court on the west, there were four at the highway and two at the court.
public_domain_references.web: For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
public_domain_references.asv: For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.
public_domain_references.kjv: At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, [and] two at Parbar.
public_domain_references.brenton: to relieve guard, also for Osa westward after the chamber-gate, three. [There was] a ward over against the ward of the ascent eastward, six [men] in a day, and four for the north, and four for the south, and at the Esephim two to relieve guard, and four by the west, and two to relieve guard at the pathway.

pob.text: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers for the sons of the Korahites and for the sons of Merari[a].

spob.text: These were the assigned groups of gatekeepers from the Korahite clan and from the descendants of Merari.

public_domain_references.bsb: These were the divisions of the gatekeepers who were descendants of Korah and Merari.
public_domain_references.web: These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
public_domain_references.asv: These were the courses of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
public_domain_references.kjv: These [are] the divisions of the porters among the sons of Kore, and among the sons of Merari.
public_domain_references.brenton: These [are] the divisions of the porters for the sons of Core, and to the sons of Merari.

pob.text: And of the Levites[b][a], Ahijah was over the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the holy things.

spob.text: Among the Levites[a], Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of things set apart as holy.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now their fellow Levites were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated things.
public_domain_references.web: Of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
public_domain_references.asv: And of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God, and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And of the Levites, Ahijah [was] over the treasures of the house of God, and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Levites their brethren [were] over the treasures of the house of the Lord, and over the treasures of the hallowed things.

pob.text: The sons of Ladan[b][a], the sons of the Gershonite belonging to Ladan: the heads of the fathers’ houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite were Jehieli.

spob.text: The descendants of Ladan belonged to the Gershonite clan. The leaders of their ancestral families were from the family line of Jehieli.

public_domain_references.bsb: From the descendants of Ladan, who were Gershonites through Ladan and heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite, were Jehieli,
public_domain_references.web: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
public_domain_references.asv: The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ [houses] belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
public_domain_references.kjv: [As concerning] the sons of Laadan; the sons of the Gershonite Laadan, chief fathers, [even] of Laadan the Gershonite, [were] Jehieli.
public_domain_references.brenton: These [were] the sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gersonite: to Ladan [belonged] the heads of the families: [the son] of Ladan the Gersonite [was] Jeiel.

pob.text: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and Joel his brother were over the treasuries of the house of Yahweh[a].

spob.text: Jehieli’s sons, Zetham and his brother Joel, were in charge of Yahweh’s temple treasuries.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: the sons of Jehieli, Zetham, and his brother Joel. They were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of Yahweh’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of the house of Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: The sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel his brother, [which were] over the treasures of the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.brenton: The sons of Jeiel [were] Zethom, and Joel; brethren [who were] over the treasures of the house of the Lord.

spob.text: For the clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel:[a]

pob.text: And Shebuel son of Gershom[a], son of Moses[b], was chief over the treasuries.

spob.text: Shebuel, the son of Gershom and grandson of Moses, was the chief officer in charge of the treasuries.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the officer in charge of the treasuries.
public_domain_references.web: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries.

pob.text: And his brothers belonging to Eliezer: Rehabiah his son[a], and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.

spob.text: His brothers from Eliezer’s branch of the family were Rehabiah, Eliezer’s son; Jeshaiah, Rehabiah’s son; Joram, Jeshaiah’s son; Zichri, Joram’s son; and Shelomith, Zichri’s son.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: His relatives through Eliezer included Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.
public_domain_references.web: His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.

public_domain_references.kjv: And his brethren by Eliezer; Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Rabias [was] son to his brother Eliezer, and [so was] Josias, and Joram, and Zechri, and Salomoth.

spob.text: Shelomoth and his brothers were responsible for all the treasuries that held the sacred items. These items had been dedicated by King David, the family heads[a], the commanders over units of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders.

public_domain_references.web: This Shelomoth and his brothers were over all the treasuries of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, had dedicated.
public_domain_references.asv: This Shelomoth and his brethren were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ [houses], the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the host, had dedicated.
public_domain_references.kjv: Which Shelomith and his brethren [were] over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the chief fathers, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the host, had dedicated.

pob.text: From the wars and from the spoil they had dedicated things to strengthen the house of Yahweh.

spob.text: They had dedicated things from the wars and from the goods taken in battle to strengthen Yahweh’s house.

public_domain_references.bsb: They had dedicated some of the plunder from their battles to the repair of the house of the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: They dedicated some of the plunder won in battles to repair Yahweh’s house.
public_domain_references.asv: Out of the spoil won in battles did they dedicate to repair the house of Jehovah.
public_domain_references.kjv: Out of the spoils won in battles did they dedicate to maintain the house of the LORD.

pob.text: And all that Samuel the seer[a], Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner[b], and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated—everything that anyone had dedicated—was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.

spob.text: Shelomith and his brothers were responsible for everything that Samuel the seer,[a] Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated—and for everything anyone had dedicated.

public_domain_references.bsb: Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah, along with everything else that was dedicated, was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
public_domain_references.web: All that Samuel the seer, Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth and of his brothers.
public_domain_references.asv: And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated, whosoever had dedicated anything, it was under the hand of Shelomoth, and of his brethren.
public_domain_references.kjv: And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated; [and] whosoever had dedicated [any thing, it was] under the hand of Shelomith, and of his brethren.
public_domain_references.brenton: and over all the holy things of God dedicated by Samuel the prophet, and Saul the son of Kis, and Abenner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Saruia, whatsoever they sanctified [was] by the hand of Salomoth and his brethren.

pob.text: For the Izharites[a], Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to the outside work over Israel, as officers and judges.

spob.text: Among the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to work outside the sanctuary, overseeing the people of Israel as officials and judges.

public_domain_references.web: Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed to the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.

public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons [were] for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the Issaarites, Chonenia, and [his] sons [were over] the outward ministration over Israel, to record and to judge.

pob.text: For the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his brothers[a], 1,700 capable men, were in charge of the oversight of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.

spob.text: For the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers—1,700 capable men—were responsible for overseeing Israel west of the Jordan. Their oversight covered all the work of Yahweh and the king’s service.

public_domain_references.bsb: From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, 1,700 capable men, had charge of the affairs of Israel west of the Jordan for all the work of the LORD and for the service of the king.
public_domain_references.web: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Yahweh and for the service of the king.
public_domain_references.asv: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valor, a thousand and seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Jehovah, and for the service of the king.
public_domain_references.kjv: [And] of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, [were] officers among them of Israel on this side Jordan westward in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the Chebronites, Asabias and his brethren, a thousand and seven hundred mighty men, [were] over the charge of Israel beyond Jordan westward, for all the service of the Lord and work of the king.

pob.text: For the Hebronites[a], Jeriah was the chief of the Hebronites according to his generations by fathers’ houses. In the fortieth year of David’s reign they were sought out[c][b], and among them mighty men of valor were found at Jazer of Gilead.

spob.text: Among the Hebronites, Jeriah was the chief, according to their family lines and ancestral clans. In the fortieth year of David’s reign, they were identified through a careful search. At Jazer in Gilead, men of great strength and ability were found among them.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: As for the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to the genealogies of his ancestors. In the fortieth year of David’s reign the records were searched, and strong, capable men were found among the Hebronites at Jazer in Gilead.
public_domain_references.web: Of the Hebronites, Jerijah was the chief of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They were sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead.
public_domain_references.asv: Of the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ [houses]. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valor at Jazer of Gilead.
public_domain_references.kjv: Among the Hebronites [was] Jerijah the chief, [even] among the Hebronites, according to the generations of his fathers. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valour at Jazer of Gilead.
public_domain_references.brenton: Of the [family] of Chebron Urias [was] chief, even of the Chebronites according to their generations, according to their families. In the fortieth year of his reign they were numbered, and there were found mighty men among them in Jazer of Galaad.

pob.text: And his brothers[a], valiant men, were two thousand seven hundred heads of fathers’ houses; and King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter of God and of the king.

spob.text: His 2,700 brothers were valiant men who led their ancestral families. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. They were responsible for all matters concerning God and all matters concerning the king.

public_domain_references.bsb: Among Jerijah’s relatives there were 2,700 capable men who were heads of families. King David appointed them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter pertaining to God and to the affairs of the king.
public_domain_references.web: His relatives, men of valor, were two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom King David made overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king.
public_domain_references.asv: And his brethren, men of valor, were two thousand and seven hundred, heads of fathers’ [houses], whom king David made overseers over the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.
public_domain_references.kjv: And his brethren, men of valour, [were] two thousand and seven hundred chief fathers, whom king David made rulers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, for every matter pertaining to God, and affairs of the king.
public_domain_references.brenton: And his brethren [were] two thousand seven hundred mighty men, chiefs of their families, and king David set them over the Rubenites, and the Gaddites, and the half-tribe of Manasse, for every ordinance of the Lord, and business of the king.

pob.text: The sons of Israel according to their number—the heads of fathers’ houses[a], and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds[c][b], and their officers who served the king in every matter of the divisions that came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—each division was twenty-four thousand.

spob.text: The Israelites were counted and organized into divisions. Their family heads,[a] commanders over thousands and hundreds, and officers served the king in all matters concerning these divisions. Each division numbered 24,000. Month by month throughout the year, one division came in for duty as another went out.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the list of the Israelites—the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in every matter concerning the divisions on rotating military duty each month throughout the year. There were 24,000 men in each division:
public_domain_references.web: Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of fathers’ households and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in any matter of the divisions which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every division were twenty-four thousand.
public_domain_references.asv: Now the children of Israel after their number, [to wit], the heads of fathers’ [houses] and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers that served the king, in any matter of the courses which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every course were twenty and four thousand.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now the children of Israel after their number, [to wit], the chief fathers and captains of thousands and hundreds, and their officers that served the king in any matter of the courses, which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year, of every course [were] twenty and four thousand.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now the sons of Israel according to their number, heads of families, captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, and scribes ministering to the king, and for every affair of the king according to [their] divisions, [for] every ordinance of coming in and going out monthly, for all the months of the year, one division of them [was] twenty-four thousand.

pob.text: Then David assembled at Jerusalem all the leaders of Israel: the leaders of the tribes[a], the leaders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the leaders over all the property and livestock belonging to the king and to his sons, together with the officials, the mighty men, and every mighty man of valor.

pob.text: Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless Yahweh your God.” And all the assembly blessed Yahweh, the God of their fathers, and bowed their heads and prostrated themselves before Yahweh and before the king.

spob.text: Then David said to everyone gathered there, “Now give praise to Yahweh your God.”[a] So they all praised Yahweh, the God of their fathers. They bowed their heads and lay facedown before Yahweh and before the king.[b]

pob.text: They sacrificed sacrifices to Yahweh and offered up burnt offerings to Yahweh on the next day after that day: one thousand bulls[a], one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, and their drink offerings[c][b], and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.

spob.text: The next day, they offered sacrifices to Yahweh. They also offered these burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, along with the liquid offerings poured out with them. They offered many more sacrifices for all Israel.[a]

pob.text: And they ate and drank before Yahweh on that day with great joy[a], and they made Solomon son of David king a second time, and they anointed him for Yahweh as ruler[d][c][b], and Zadok as priest.
